program_name: Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance
teaching_language: TRILINGUAL (Italian / German / English) — NOT an English-taught programme. The admission-information PDF states unambiguously: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' The programme page and brochure 'At a glance' box both say 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)'. Crucially, unibz's own guidance for trilingual masters states the admission premise: 'In order to be admitted to your Master's degree course, you have met the entry language requirements, i.e. you have demonstrated that you can use at least two of the three official teaching languages at C1 and B2 level.' ACTUAL LANGUAGE DISTRIBUTION of the published course offering (cohorts enrolled from 2025, both curricula pooled, 151 CP of listed courses): ENGLISH ~96 CP (Economic Policy and Sustainable Development 6; Public Management and Innovation 6; Introduction to Data Management and Data Analysis 8; Public and Administrative Law 8; Policy Design, Democracy and Citizen Engagement 8; Applied Regression Analysis for Public Policy 6; Economics of the Public Sector 6; Behavioral Economics and Public Policy Design 6; Project Design and Management 6; Strategies for Sustainable Solutions: Design Thinking in Public Services 6; Sustainability Economics 6; Impact Evaluation 6; Energy and Resource Economics 6; Labour, Health and Education 6; Finance of the Public Sector 6). ITALIAN ~37 CP (Information and Digitalization LAB 3; Accounting in the Public Sector 6; Administrative Law and Writing LAB 6; Soft Skills and Problem Solving Clinic 4; Law of Regions and Autonomies 6; European Administrative Law and Projects 6; Contracts and Sustainability 6). GERMAN ~18 CP (Human Resource Management in the Public Sector 6; Law and Policy of European and International Organizations 6; Non-profits and Cooperatives 6). So English is the single largest language of instruction by volume — roughly 64% of the offered credits — which makes this programme LOOK English-friendly at course level. That impression is misleading: the language BARRIER here is administrative (the C1 + B2 entry rule and the C1/C1/B1 exit rule), not the timetable. majors_tracks_study_plans:
TWO CURRICULA (unibz calls them 'streams' on the programme page and 'curricula' in the study-plan pages). Students choose one; the choice materially changes the language burden, which is the single most important thing an English-speaking applicant needs to know about this programme.

(1) PUBLIC POLICY, IMPACT AND SUSTAINABILITY — 'focus on impactful policy tools, grounded on economic principles with a strong emphasis on analytical and quantitative skills essential for evidence-based decision making.' Year 1: Policy, Management, and Innovation in the Public Sector 12 CP (M-1 Economic Policy and Sustainable Development 6 + M-2 Public Management and Innovation 6); Introduction to Data Management and Data Analysis 8; Public and Administrative Law 8; Policy Design, Democracy and Citizen Engagement 8; Information and Digitalization LAB 3; Applied Regression Analysis for Public Policy 6; Economics and Public Policy Design 12 (M-1 Economics of the Public Sector 6 + M-2 Behavioral Economics and Public Policy Design 6). Year 2: Project Development and Sustainability 12 (M-1 Project Design and Management 6 + M-2 Strategies for Sustainable Solutions: Design Thinking in Public Services 6); Soft Skills and Problem Solving Clinic 4; Free choice 12; Sustainability Economics 6; Complementary subjects 18 (three of: Impact Evaluation 6, Energy and Resource Economics 6, Non-profits and Cooperatives 6, Labour, Health and Education 6); Final thesis 11.

(2) GOVERNANCE, LAW AND MANAGEMENT — 'focus on the implementation of public policies combining legal, administrative, and managerial perspectives.' Year 1: Policy, Management, and Innovation in the Public Sector 12 (same two modules); Introduction to Data Management and Data Analysis 8; Public and Administrative Law 8; Policy Design, Democracy and Citizen Engagement 8; Information and Digitalization LAB 3; Accounting in the Public Sector 6; Law for Public Institutions 12 (M-1 Administrative Law and Writing LAB 6 + M-2 Law and Policy of European and International Organizations 6). Year 2: Project Development and Sustainability 12; Soft Skills and Problem Solving Clinic 4; Free Choice 12; Human Resource Management in the Public Sector 6; Complementary subjects 18 (three of: Law of Regions and Autonomies 6, European Administrative Law and Projects 6, Contracts and Sustainability 6, Finance of the Public Sector 6); Final Thesis 11.

LANGUAGE CONSEQUENCE OF THE CHOICE (computed from the published course-language codes): in PUBLIC POLICY, IMPACT AND SUSTAINABILITY roughly 72 CP of compulsory teaching is in English and only 7 CP is compulsorily in Italian (Information and Digitalization LAB 3 + Soft Skills and Problem Solving Clinic 4), and the 18 CP of complementary subjects can be chosen entirely in English — so a student could complete close to the whole degree in English. In GOVERNANCE, LAW AND MANAGEMENT roughly 19 CP of compulsory teaching is in Italian (Information and Digitalization LAB 3, Accounting in the Public Sector 6, Administrative Law and Writing LAB 6, Soft Skills Clinic 4) and 12 CP in German (Law and Policy of European and International Organizations 6, Human Resource Management in the Public Sector 6), and three of the four complementary options are Italian-taught. This second curriculum is unusable without real Italian and German. NO other variants exist: no dual-study track, no four-year variant, no distance option. PART-TIME ENROLMENT is available — 'Students choose this option after enrollment (in October) and not during the application.' Degree Course Director: Prof. Stefania Baroncelli (stefania.baroncelli@unibz.it); Administrative Secretary: Marina Fattor (marina.fattor2@unibz.it). english_only_accessibility:
EFFECTIVELY CLOSED for a candidate who speaks only English. This confirms the working note on the source list, and the evidence is unusually strong — it is both a rule and a measured outcome.

THE RULE. Entry requires C1 in a first language AND B2 in a second language, chosen from Italian, German and English only. A candidate whose only qualifying language is English can satisfy the C1 first-language slot but has nothing to put in the B2 second-language slot. The admission PDF is explicit that this is eliminatory: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' The signed ranking-list decree restates it in Italian: 'Al corso di laurea magistrale hanno accesso le persone che sono in possesso di buone competenze in due delle tre lingue di insegnamento (tedesco, italiano o inglese); nella prima lingua le competenze devono essere ad un livello C1 …, nella seconda ad un livello B2.' unibz's trilingual-master guidance says the same from the student's side: 'you have demonstrated that you can use at least two of the three official teaching languages at C1 and B2 level.'

THE MEASURED OUTCOME (2026/27, from the two signed ranking lists). Early Bird: 6 EU/parity applicants were excluded solely for failing the language requirements, and in the non-EU pool only ONE applicant was admitted while THREE were excluded for language — i.e. 3 of the 4 non-EU applicants who reached the ranking stage were eliminated by the language gate alone. Late Application: a further 6 EU applicants excluded for language, plus 1 more excluded for incomplete documents combined with language. That is 16 documented language exclusions across two sessions on a programme admitting 68 people — a far higher language-attrition rate than unibz's English-taught masters (Computing for Data Science recorded only 2 and 1).

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT OPEN. Only acquiring a genuine B2 in Italian or German before the application deadline. There are exactly two practical routes: a recognised certificate (Italian: CELI 3-B2, CILS DUE-B2, PLIDA B2, telc Italiano B2; German: Goethe-Zertifikat B2, ÖSD B2, telc Deutsch B2, TestDaF with TDN 4 in all parts), or a B2 exam sat at the unibz Language Centre during one of the published registration windows. Reaching B2 from zero is a 1–2 year project, so for the 2026/27 or 2027/28 cycle this is not a realistic pivot for an English-only candidate.

EVEN IF ADMITTED, GRADUATION IS GATED. Exit requires C1 in the first language, C1 in the second AND B1 in the third — so an English-only entrant would have to certify both Italian and German (one at C1, one at B1) to graduate. There is no exemption. VERDICT: effectively-closed. Do not present this programme to an English-only applicant as an option; the Faculty of Economics and Management's genuinely English-accessible masters (e.g. Data Analytics for Economics and Management, Accounting and Finance — check each separately) are the correct alternatives, as are the Faculty of Engineering's English-taught masters.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a merit-based ranking list produced purely by DOCUMENTARY EVALUATION of the applicant's academic dossier. There is NO entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO CENT-S, NO GMAT/GRE, NO interview, NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video and NO project proposal. The ranking decree describes the method as 'la valutazione dei dossiers di aspiranti studenti e studentesse' — evaluation of applicant dossiers — against criteria approved by Faculty Council of the Faculty of Economics resolution no. 200 of 14.11.2025. Selection has two gates: (a) an eliminatory prerequisite gate — a qualifying bachelor degree (or 16 ECTS across at least two named disciplinary areas), plus the C1 + B2 language requirement, plus a minimum total of 60/100 points; and (b) a scored ranking worth up to 102 points. Separate ranking lists are drawn for (i) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (ii) non-EU citizens living abroad, each against its own quota. LANGUAGE EXAMS at the unibz Language Centre are the only test-like element, and only for applicants who choose that route to prove their levels.

Admission is decided entirely on uploaded documents. Published 2026/27 dates (all online): EARLY BIRD — 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); LATE APPLICATION — 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). selection_scoring:
MAXIMUM 102 POINTS, awarded on documents only, with an eliminatory floor of 60.

(1) GRADE AVERAGE — max 70 points. 'If you have already graduated: Final grade, given in xx/30. If you have not graduated yet: The grade average of the passed university exams given in xx/30.' Foreign applicants must supply the grading scale of their home university (minimum pass grade and maximum achievable grade) so the mark can be converted to the Italian /30 scale.
(2) SUMMA CUM LAUDE BONUS — +2 points: 'In case of a bachelor concluded with the highest grade and the mention "summa cum laude", 2 additional points will be awarded.'
(3) FURTHER LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY — 10 points, all-or-nothing: 'You will receive 10 points if you demonstrate a B2 level in the third language.' Both unibz-recognised certificates and unibz Language Centre exam passes count.
(4) PRIOR KNOWLEDGE — max 20 points, for having completed or being about to complete a bachelor in L-14, L-16, L-18, L-33, L-36 or L-37 (D.M. 270/04), or 02, 15, 17, 19, 28 or 31 (D.M. 509/99), or a law master LMG/01 (D.M. 270/04) or 22/S (D.M. 509/99), or an equivalent recognised foreign degree, or a pre-1999 Italian degree judged equivalent. ALTERNATIVELY — max 10 points 'if you have successfully attended one or more courses in disciplinary fields/scientific sectors coherent with the course offering of the subjects taught in this master programme (also at other universities)', with the explicit carve-out that 'The 16 credit points (ECTS) required for admission to the master will not be considered' for these 10 points. Note the asymmetry: applicants from the six named policy/law/economics bachelor classes can score 20, everyone else is capped at 10 — a 10-point structural penalty for e.g. an engineering or humanities graduate.

ELIMINATORY FLOOR: 'Minimum total points for admission to the ranking list: 60 points.' The signed decree words it as 'il punteggio minimo di 60/100 punti' — note the decree says 60/100 even though the four criteria sum to 102; treat 60 as the absolute floor. 'The total score will be adjusted upwards or downwards' (rounded).

TIE-BREAK: 'In the event of equal scores, priority will be given to the applicant who has obtained the highest score for the first criterion' (i.e. the grade average, the most heavily weighted criterion, per art. 26 para. 2 lett. b) of the admission regulation in force). 'If scores are still equal, the younger applicant will have priority.'

ACTUAL 2026/27 COMPETITION LEVEL (from the two signed ranking lists). EARLY BIRD, EU/parity: 40 admitted against 40 places — the quota was exactly filled, top score 94.91, cut-off score 66.22 at rank 40. EARLY BIRD, non-EU living abroad: only 1 admitted (score 83.84) against 5 places, with 3 further non-EU applicants excluded for language. LATE APPLICATION, EU/parity: 28 admitted, top score 102.00 (a perfect score — 70 + 2 laude + 10 language + 20 prior knowledge), cut-off 61.05 at rank 28; 1 applicant excluded for reaching neither the 16 ECTS in two areas nor the minimum score (they scored 56.37), 1 for incomplete documents plus language, and 6 for language alone. PRACTICAL READING: the EU pool is genuinely competitive at the top but the cut-off sits only just above the 60-point floor, so the real filter is the eliminatory prerequisites — especially language — rather than the score. The non-EU pool is tiny and was overwhelmingly eliminated by the language gate rather than by score.
bonus_points: Three additive bonus mechanisms exist, none of them the ones used elsewhere at unibz. (1) SUMMA CUM LAUDE — a flat +2 points 'In case of a bachelor concluded with the highest grade and the mention "summa cum laude"'. (2) THIRD-LANGUAGE B2 — a flat 10 points for certifying B2 in the language that is NOT one of the two used to meet the entry requirement. This is the highest-leverage discretionary item in the whole rubric: it is worth 10 of 102 points (~10%), it is all-or-nothing, and it is the only criterion an applicant can still improve after starting the application, by sitting a unibz Language Centre B2 exam in the relevant registration window. (3) PRIOR KNOWLEDGE — up to 20 points for holding (or being about to hold) a degree in one of the named law / administration / economics / political-science bachelor classes or a law master (LMG/01, 22/S), falling to a maximum of 10 points for anyone whose relevant background consists only of individual coherent courses. There is NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that mechanism belongs to the Faculty of Engineering masters — Software Engineering and Computing for Data Science). There is NO GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), NO startup-project bonus (Entrepreneurship and Innovation) and NO extracurricular-activities bonus (a bachelor-level mechanism). Consequently the prestige of the applicant's previous university is worth nothing here — only the grade, the degree class and the third language.
portfolio_and_materials: NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video, NO project proposal, NO reference letters and NO CV are required. None of these instruments are used by this programme, so no page limits, character limits or file-size caps exist. Only three upload categories are specified in the application portal: (1) THE QUALIFICATION DOSSIER — if graduated in Italy, the diploma supplement or a self-declaration under Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000 of the degree awarded with the exams passed; if graduated abroad, the diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed, or, if not yet graduated, the transcript of records — in Italian, German or English. The dossier 'must contain the following information: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)', and for foreign qualifications also 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)'. 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' (2) THE EXCEL FILE — required ONLY of applicants who have not yet graduated: 'If you have not graduated yet, you must confirm that you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS) in your course of origin. Please use the excel file available in the application portal.' Unlike the Faculty of Engineering masters, this Excel is conditional, not universal, and its purpose is narrow: proving the 140-ECTS threshold. (3) OPTIONAL LANGUAGE CERTIFICATES, uploaded to claim the 10-point third-language bonus. Plus, at account level, a valid ID card or passport front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. Once submitted the application cannot be modified, and 'Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'
interview: NO INTERVIEW. This programme does not use an interview at any stage, for any category of applicant, in any of the three application sessions. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF nor either signed ranking-list decree contains any reference to a colloquio / Gespräch / interview, and neither ranking list has the 'did not attend the interviews' exclusion category that appears, for example, in the Master in Computing for Data Science lists. Selection is 100% documentary. There is also no low-grade trigger: unlike the engineering masters (which interview candidates below 24/30), this programme sets no minimum grade average at all — a weak average simply produces a low score against the 70-point criterion and, if the total falls under 60, exclusion from the ranking list.
conditional_admission:
THREE distinct conditional regimes.

(1) NOT YET GRADUATED — the threshold is 140 ECTS, not the 120 used by most unibz masters: 'You can apply if you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS). In this case you will be admitted conditionally, and you will need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' The decree records these applicants with an asterisk in the ranking list: 'al momento della preiscrizione queste persone non erano ancora in possesso del titolo di studio e pertanto sono ammesse con riserva e devono conseguire il titolo di studio entro la scadenza prevista per l'immatricolazione (13 ottobre 2026 ore 12 mezzogiorno)' — they must obtain the degree by 13/10/2026 at noon. In the 2026/27 Early Bird list 18 of the 40 admitted EU applicants carried this asterisk; in the Late list 8 of 28 did. IF YOU GRADUATE LATE: 'You cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list. In this case you should not pay the tuition fees to secure your admission.' A late enrolment request may then be submitted and, 'only if there still are available places', enrolment is possible by 11 DECEMBER 2026 (2026-12-11).

(2) ADMISSION WITH RESERVATION FOR MISSING QUALIFICATION — 'If you do not have the required academic qualification, you will be given a conditional offer for a study place and you must submit your qualification upon enrolment.' Even after enrolment: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'

(3) NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD are provisionally admitted as a class. The decree states: 'I cittadini e le cittadine non-UE residenti all'estero sono ammessi e ammesse con riserva: la riserva viene sciolta previa comunicazione ufficiale, inviata direttamente all'unibz, dal consolato italiano all'estero' — the reservation is lifted only once the Italian consulate abroad sends the official communication directly to unibz. The single non-EU applicant admitted in the 2026/27 Early Bird list carried BOTH this reservation and the not-yet-graduated asterisk.
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE — no OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) mechanism exists for this programme. OFA is an undergraduate instrument at unibz, assigned to bachelor candidates who fail the compulsory mathematics test (Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics, Tourism Sport and Event Management). At master level the equivalent quality gate is handled entirely BEFORE admission, through three eliminatory prerequisites: the qualifying degree class or the 16 ECTS in at least two disciplinary areas; the C1 + B2 language requirement; and the 60-point minimum total score. Neither the admission-information PDF nor either signed ranking list mentions OFA, and no ranking entry carries an OFA marker. The one post-admission remedial obligation that DOES exist here is linguistic rather than academic: students who cannot certify their third language must sit a placement test after admission and follow an assigned Language Centre learning path towards B1, which gates their ability to sit exams in that language.
language_requirements:
This is the decisive field for this programme and the reason it is effectively closed to English-only applicants.

CORE RULE, quoted: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) — 1st language: C1; 2nd language: B2; 3rd language: no level required. A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language. Exit level (to graduate) — 1st language: C1; 2nd language: C1; 3rd language: B1. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.'

HOW POSITIONS ARE DEFINED: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Positions are assigned by proficiency, not by which language it is — so English can occupy the 1st, 2nd or 3rd slot depending on the individual.

CERTIFICATION OBLIGATION: 'The certification is mandatory for the first and second language, for the third language it is recommended (from B1 onwards).' Administrative distinction: a final certificate awarded by an ITALIAN PUBLIC INSTITUTION requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a FOREIGN PUBLIC INSTITUTION requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original diploma. Proof is submitted in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'.

EXAM REGISTRATION CONSTRAINT: 'you can only register for C1 and B2 level exams and only for one level per language (e.g. in the same exam session you can register for a C1 German and a B2 Italian exam, but not for a C1 and a B2 German exam).'

THIRD LANGUAGE AFTER ADMISSION: students who cannot certify the third language sit a placement test and are assigned a learning path towards B1. 'If you are an absolute beginner in the third language, or if you have a level below B1, you may attend a three-week intensive language course during the pre-semester session in September.' Critically, 'Beginner courses (A1) will be offered exclusively during the pre-semester intensive course session in September [and] will no longer be offered during the academic year. Therefore, absolute beginners should start their learning path for the third language by attending the intensive courses in September' (01–18/09/2026). Language Centre courses are free of charge; extensive courses run 4 h/week during semesters and intensive courses 8 h/week between semesters, and unibz warns: 'Our experience and data demonstrate that it is very difficult to reach the required language levels without completing your learning path.'

ENFORCEMENT IN PRACTICE (2026/27): 6 EU/parity applicants excluded for language in the Early Bird session, plus 3 of the 4 non-EU applicants; 6 more EU applicants excluded for language in the Late session, plus 1 for incomplete documents combined with language. Sixteen documented language exclusions in one admission cycle.
entry_levels_by_position: C1 / B2 / no level required — the standard unibz trilingual master pattern, and one notch harder than the trilingual bachelor pattern. Position is defined by the candidate's own proficiency, not by the identity of the language: the 1st language is whichever of Italian, German or English the candidate is strongest in (must be C1), the 2nd is the next strongest (must be B2), and the 3rd is the weakest (no entry requirement). Comparison across unibz: Bachelor in Computer Science B2/B2/none; Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering B2/B1/none; this programme and the Master in Accounting and Finance C1/B2/none; English-taught masters such as Computing for Data Science B2/none/none. So this is at the strict end of the unibz scale — the C1 in the first language is a full CEFR level above the bachelor entry bar, and the mandatory B2 in a SECOND of the three teaching languages is the clause that excludes monolingual English speakers. For a typical Turkish applicant, English would occupy the 1st position at C1 (usually via an English-medium degree or high school, recognised as C1, or an IELTS 7.0–8.0 / TOEFL iBT 95–113 / Cambridge C1 Advanced certificate), leaving Italian or German to be certified at B2 — the position that cannot be filled without genuine prior study. Note that although the 3rd language has no ENTRY level, B1 in it is required to sit curricular examinations taught in that language, and B1 is an EXIT requirement.
exit_levels: C1 / C1 / B1 — a full graduation language requirement, and one of the strictest at unibz. Quoted from the admission PDF: 'Exit level (to graduate) — 1st language: C1; 2nd language: C1; 3rd language: B1.' unibz's trilingual-master guidance restates it: 'there are exit language requirements: in order to graduate, you will need to certify two languages at the C1 level and the third language at the B1 level.' The practical consequence is that admission does not settle the language problem — a student admitted with C1 + B2 must still RAISE the second language from B2 to C1 and BUILD the third language from scratch (or from whatever level the placement test finds) up to certified B1, all while completing 120 ECTS in two years. unibz explicitly plans for this: the recommended learning path for an absolute beginner in the third language runs Intensive A1.1–A1.2 in September (90 h) → Extensive A2.1 in semester 1 (40 h) → Intensive A2.2 in February (60 h) → Extensive B1.1a in semester 2 (40 h) → Intensive B1.1b–B1.2a–B1.2b in July (60 h), i.e. roughly 290 contact hours across the first year, with the B1 exam sat at the end of July / beginning of August and a 'B1 round up' intensive course in September for those who fail. For the second language, 'you can attend an intensive C1.1–C1.2 course in September and continue with C1.3 … in the 1st semester of the 2nd year.' Crucially: 'Taking part in a language course and passing the relevant end-of-course test doesn't mean that you have certified your level. To certify your language proficiency, you must either take a language proficiency exam at the Language Centre or submit a language certificate recognised by unibz.' Failure to certify the exit levels means failure to graduate; there is no exemption or waiver published.
third_language_exam_threshold: APPLICABLE and enforced. Quoted from the admission PDF: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language.' unibz's trilingual-master page repeats it: 'The Master's degree course in which you are enrolled includes a B1 level in the third language which must be achieved in order to register for the examinations of curricular courses taught in that language.' Because this programme runs roughly 37 CP of Italian-taught and 18 CP of German-taught courses, the B1 gate has real bite: a student whose third language is Italian cannot sit the Information and Digitalization LAB (3 CP), Soft Skills and Problem Solving Clinic (4 CP), Accounting in the Public Sector (6 CP), Administrative Law and Writing LAB (6 CP), Law of Regions and Autonomies (6 CP), European Administrative Law and Projects (6 CP) or Contracts and Sustainability (6 CP) until B1 is certified — and several of those are COMPULSORY in the Governance, Law and Management curriculum. B1 is also an exit requirement in its own right. Sequencing: students who cannot certify the third language at admission take a placement test after admission ('You will receive further information about the test by e-mail'), are assigned a learning path accordingly, and are aimed at B1 'after the first study year'. Absolute beginners must start with the September pre-semester intensive courses (01–18/09/2026), because A1 modules are offered ONLY in that September window. Additionally, certifying B2 (not merely B1) in the third language is worth 10 points in the admission ranking — so the third language is both a graduation gate and a scoring lever.
proof_pathways:
FOUR recognised ways to prove a language level, all handled inside the application portal.

(1) MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF THE FINAL HIGH-SCHOOL YEAR, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1. Special case: 'Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian.' For foreign qualifications: 'If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your hign school diploma [sic], please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.'

(2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE IN ITALIAN, GERMAN OR ENGLISH — recognised as C1. unibz graduates 'must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1)'. For foreign qualifications: 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' This is the standard route by which a Turkish graduate of an English-medium programme obtains C1 English — but it produces only ONE qualifying language, which is exactly the problem.

(3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list. 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.' Practical B2 options for the second language — ITALIAN: CELI 3-B2, CILS DUE-B2, PLIDA B2, telc Italiano B2; GERMAN: Goethe-Zertifikat B2, ÖSD B2, telc Deutsch B2, TestDaF (minimum TDN 4 in all parts), DSH-1 and above. C1 options for the first language — ENGLISH: IELTS (General and Academic) 7.0–8.0, TOEFL iBT 95–113, PTE Academic 76–84, PTE General Level 4, LanguageCert General C1 / Academic C1 / ESOL C1, Aptis ESOL Advanced C1, Cambridge C1 Advanced; ITALIAN: CELI 4-C1, CILS TRE-C1, PLIDA C1; GERMAN: Goethe-Zertifikat C1, ÖSD C1, telc Deutsch C1, DSH-2/DSH-3.

(4) LANGUAGE EXAMS ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, registered online through the portal under 'enrol for language exams'. 2026/27 dates: Early Bird 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026) and 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); Late 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). SEQUENCING TRAP, quoted: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' Only C1 and B2 levels can be registered, one level per language per session. Applicants in the Additional Application Session have no Language Centre exam window and must rely on routes 1–3.

ADDITIONAL PATHWAY FOR FOREIGN / BILINGUAL SCHOOLS: 'If the foreign language proficiency levels (for German, Italian, or English) are explicitly indicated on the diploma of graduation according to the Common European Framework of Reference (i.e., B1, B2 or C1), and if all four language abilities (reading, listening, speaking, writing) have been assessed, then the indicated levels will be accepted as a proof of proficiency for the second and/or third language.' The school-leaving certificate must be uploaded under the relevant language and 'The Language Centre will decide on its recognition.' This is a genuine second-language route for applicants from bilingual or international schools that certify CEFR levels in German or Italian on the diploma itself.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026, 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants' (a trilingual DE/IT/EN document). General dispositions, quoted from the English column: a certificate must '1. include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and '2. indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade (and/or the detailed assessment is indicated on the certificate itself or by appropriate documentation faithful to the original by the certification organisation)'. Further binding rules: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed' — the WEAKEST sub-skill sets the level; 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation'; 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list'; 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted' — a certificate cannot be assembled from several providers; 'Certificates of participation, certificates of end-of-course-tests and examinations from private educational institutions as well as results of placement tests will not be recognised'; 'Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff will not be recognised'; 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January' — i.e. a certificate issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year remains valid for the whole of the current year. Entries in the 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' section have unlimited validity. [uncertain] — the home-edition exception: an asterisk defined as '* Also accepted as "home edition"' appears against several major English tests in the extracted table (IELTS, TOEFL/TOEIC, LanguageCert Academic and others), which would mean their at-home variants ARE accepted; because this is rendered from a complex multi-column PDF table the asterisk's exact per-cell scope could not be confirmed cell by cell, and no equivalent asterisk was observed against the Italian or German providers. An applicant relying on an at-home test should confirm with language.centre@unibz.it before applying. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu:
THREE sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). Every deadline falls at NOON local time, not midnight.
• EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03/2026 – 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28.
• LATE APPLICATION (EU only): 28/05/2026 – 08/07/2026 = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08.
• ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September only where places remain): 18/08/2026 – 04/09/2026 = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04.
The Additional Session IS confirmed open for this programme — the official Additional Application Session page lists 'Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance' with '(Application possible)'. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and 'If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one'; the Early Bird decree confirms this for language-excluded applicants ('Possono ricandidarsi nella seconda sessione' — they may reapply in the second session). As of the 2026-08-29 verification date the Early Bird and Late sessions have closed with signed ranking lists published, and only the Additional Session remains open, closing 2026-09-04 at noon — this is time-critical and must be re-checked before use.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03/2026 – 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. The admission-information PDF is explicit: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session — both are labelled 'only for EU citizens'. They are ranked on a separate list against a separate quota of just 5 places and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT WITHOUT AN ITALIAN RESIDENCE PERMIT: exactly one attempt per academic year, closing at the end of April — five months before teaching starts — against 5 places, with a hard C1 + B2 language gate that eliminated 3 of the 4 non-EU applicants in the 2026/27 cycle. Missing the window means waiting a full year.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants, and the second is the one that matters most to Turkish and other non-EU nationals already in Italy. (1) 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State.' (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay.' EXPLICIT EXCLUSION: 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid.' If the permit has expired, a renewal request must be attached. CRITICAL WARNING, quoted: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The signed decree restates it: a non-EU applicant who declares Italian residence but does not attach a valid residence permit 'viene inserito/inserita nella graduatoria riservata ai cittadini e alle cittadine non-UE residenti all'estero' (is placed on the ranking list reserved for non-EU citizens resident abroad). WHY THIS MATTERS ENORMOUSLY HERE: the two pools are wildly asymmetric. EU/parity had 50 places and admitted 68 people across two sessions (40 + 28) with cut-off scores of 66.22 and 61.05 — barely above the 60-point floor. The non-EU pool had 5 places and admitted 1 person. A qualifying applicant who fails to upload the permit therefore moves from a pool where almost any qualifying candidate gets in, into a pool of 5 places, and simultaneously loses access to the Late and Additional sessions and incurs the €50 application fee. Establishing parity of treatment is the single highest-value administrative step available to an eligible applicant for this programme.
places_quotas: THREE separate quotas for 2026/27, published in the admission-information PDF as: 'Available places — EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application: 40; Late Application: 10. Non-EU citizens (living abroad): Early Bird Application: 5.' The programme page and brochure summarise this as 'Places available: 50 EU + 5 non-EU' (50 = 40 + 10), so the EU:non-EU ratio is 10:1 — one of the most EU-skewed allocations at unibz, and the mirror image of the Master in Computing for Data Science (30 EU + 30 non-EU). CARRY-OVER RULE: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' The carry-over benefits EU applicants only; unfilled EU places are never transferred to the non-EU pool, and the non-EU quota exists only in the Early Bird session. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE from the two signed ranking lists: Early Bird — 40 EU/parity admitted (exactly the 40-place quota; 6 further EU applicants excluded for language) and 1 non-EU admitted against 5 non-EU places (3 further non-EU applicants excluded for language); Late — 28 EU/parity admitted, with 6 excluded for language, 1 for incomplete documents plus language, and 1 for meeting neither the 16-ECTS requirement nor the 60-point minimum. Total admitted across the two published sessions: 68 EU/parity and 1 non-EU. [uncertain] — admitting 28 in the Late session against a nominal 10 late places means at least 18 Early Bird admits must have declined or failed to secure their place, with those places carried over under the rule quoted above; this is the researcher's inference from the two decrees, since unibz does not publish attrition figures. A third ranking list for the Additional Session was due by 18/09/2026 and did not exist at the verification date, so the number of places still available in that session is unknown — but the Faculty opening the session at all implies places remained.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD: ranking lists published by 27/05/2026 (2026-05-27); payment of the 1st instalment of tuition fees — €600, the payment that actually secures the place — by 05/06/2026 noon (2026-06-05); enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 13/10/2026 noon (2026-07-10 to 2026-10-13). LATE APPLICATION: ranking lists by 30/07/2026 (2026-07-30); 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon (2026-08-06); enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION: ranking lists by 18/09/2026 (2026-09-18); 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon (2026-09-25); enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. All three sessions share the same hard final enrolment deadline of 13/10/2026 at noon, which is also the deadline by which conditionally admitted applicants must have completed their bachelor. LATE-ENROLMENT SAFETY VALVE: applicants who graduate after 13/10/2026 may submit a late enrolment request and, 'only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026' (2026-12-11). GENERAL RULES: missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant in the ranking list. An applicant admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the instalment twice, but 'By confirming your place, you renounce admission to the other programmes.' Paying does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and 'If you pay but do not enrol, you are not entitled to a refund, except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country.' 'Enrolment is recommended as early as possible, so you have the possibility to upload incomplete documents before the deadline.' No waiting-list contact date is published for this programme (unlike some engineering masters), and neither 2026/27 ranking list contains a waiting-list section. APPEALS: 'Avverso il presente atto amministrativo è ammesso ricorso al Tribunale di Giustizia Amministrativa di Bolzano entro 60 giorni dalla notifica o dalla pubblicazione dello stesso' — appeal to the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of notification or publication.
programme_specific_dates: This programme has NO programme-specific admission dates beyond the standard unibz calendar — no interview dates, no test dates, no portfolio-submission dates, because none of those instruments are used. The only admission-adjacent dates are the LANGUAGE EXAM sessions at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants using that route: 16/03/2026 (registration 02–09/03/2026); 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (registration 24/03–08/04/2026); 22–26/06/2026 (registration 28/05–15/06/2026). PREPARATORY AND START-OF-YEAR DATES 2026/27: intensive language courses 01–18/09/2026 (Monday to Friday, 6 h/day — the ONLY window in which A1 beginner modules are offered, so an absolute beginner in the third language must attend); optional pre-courses 21/09–09/10/2026; Freshers Days 28–29/09/2026. ACADEMIC CALENDAR 2026/27 (Faculty of Economics and Management): 1st semester classes 28/09–23/12/2026, extraordinary exam session 10–23/12/2026, holidays 24/12/2026–06/01/2027, classes resume 07–23/01/2027, exams 25/01–20/02/2027; 2nd semester classes 01/03–25/03/2027, holidays 26–29/03/2027, classes 30/03–12/06/2027, extraordinary exam session 12–22/05/2027, exams 15/06–10/07/2027; autumn exam session 23/08–25/09/2027. IN-PROGRAMME MILESTONE: part-time enrolment is chosen after enrolment, in October, not during the application. The recommended third-language learning path also has fixed windows — Intensive A1.1–A1.2 in September, Extensive A2.1 in semester 1, Intensive A2.2 in February, Extensive B1.1a in semester 2, Intensive B1.1b–B1.2a–B1.2b in July, with the B1 exam at the end of July / beginning of August and a 'B1 round up' course in September for resitters.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION, via the portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup/ : (1) an account plus a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (2) the completed and correctly submitted online form; (3) THE QUALIFICATION DOSSIER — if graduated in Italy, the diploma supplement or a self-declaration under Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000 of the degree awarded with the exams passed (or, if not yet graduated, of the exams passed); if graduated abroad, the diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed, or the transcript of records if not yet graduated, 'in Italian, German or English'. It 'must contain the following information: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)', and for foreign qualifications also the 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)'; (4) THE EXCEL FILE, but ONLY if not yet graduated — 'you must confirm that you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS) in your course of origin. Please use the excel file available in the application portal'; (5) proof of the first and second language (mandatory) and optionally of the third language (to claim the 10 points), uploaded under 'upload language certificates' or registered under 'enrol for language exams'; (6) if the qualification was gained abroad, the diploma of the qualification — 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'; (7) for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay, plus a renewal request if it has expired. 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' Once submitted the application cannot be modified; 'Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration'; and 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must additionally upload: the degree diploma of the Bachelor; an official translation of the degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents were issued in German or English); and the Diploma Supplement, 'where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. Then the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements appropriate to the country (see credential_recognition). Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the beginning of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. Quoted from the admission-information PDF, section 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy)': 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons — pay NO application fee. In unibz's parallel documentation the same charge is described as a non-refundable administration fee. Given that the non-EU pool for this programme has only 5 places and eliminated 3 of 4 applicants on language grounds in 2026/27, an English-only non-EU applicant would be paying €50 for a near-certain exclusion; establishing parity of treatment where genuinely available removes both the fee and the bottleneck.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year, paid in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which 'includes the revenue stamp of € 16' (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, which 'must be paid by March of the following year'. 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' 'If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees.' EXEMPTIONS: 'Students with a disability recognized under article 3, paragraph 1, of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66%: the disability certificate, issued by the health authorities, must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year'; and 'Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government.' 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' At roughly €1,200 per year the programme is inexpensive by international standards and the fee is identical for EU and non-EU students — there is no differentiated international rate. For historical context, the predecessor Master in Public Policies and Administration charged €1,348.50 per year, so the fee has come DOWN. Reference pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the admission-information PDF https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/master-in-public-policy-and-innovative-governance_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: The main route is the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano (South Tyrol), administered by the Office for the Right to Study / Office for Higher Education Support. 'The Office for the Right to Study provides the following annual grants for students: ordinary study grants; merit scholarships; grants for fostering postgraduate studies.' Applications 'must be filled in and sent through the e-government service online', with assistance available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. Grant holders also recover their tuition: 'If you are able to receive a grant from the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, you receive the reimbursement of monies paid for the academic year.' CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS, quoted verbatim: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption.' The ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION IS OPEN for this programme (18/08–04/09/2026 by noon, EU citizens and parity-of-treatment applicants only) and closes within days of the verification date. (1) THE CENTRAL FINDING IS FIRM. The working note 'possibly effectively closed for an English-only candidate' is CONFIRMED and can be stated without hedging. It rests on an explicit rule (C1 in a first and B2 in a second of Italian/German/English at entry; C1/C1/B1 at exit) stated identically in the admission PDF, the programme page, the signed decrees and unibz's own trilingual-master guidance — reinforced by 16 documented language exclusions across the two published 2026/27 sessions, including 3 of the 4 non-EU applicants.

(2) COUNTER-INTUITIVE NUANCE WORTH RECORDING. Although the programme is effectively closed at the ADMISSION gate, it is unusually English-heavy at the TEACHING level: roughly 96 of 151 offered credits are delivered in English, and in the Public Policy, Impact and Sustainability curriculum only about 7 CP of compulsory teaching is in Italian. Anyone reading only the course list could wrongly conclude the programme is English-accessible. The barrier is administrative, not timetabled — a distinction that matters if unibz ever relaxes the language rule.

(3) COURSE-LANGUAGE DATA IS SECOND-ORDER. The per-course teaching languages come from the rendered course-offering page for the cohort 'enrolled from 2025' with the 2026/27 year selector, not from a downloadable PDF; the credit-by-language arithmetic is the researcher's own. Teaching languages can be reassigned between years. Flagged inline in teaching_language and majors_tracks_study_plans.

(4) RENAME TIMING IS INFERRED. The programme is definitely the successor to the 'Master in Public Policies and Administration' (same LM-63, same campus, same 50+5 quota, same language rule, whose admission PDF is still online and whose abbreviation 'ppa' still appears in a live unibz URL, and which is still named inside the 2026/27 decree). The rename took effect for cohorts from 2024/25 — inferred from the cohort page labels ('enrolled before 2024', 'enrolled from 2024', 'enrolled from 2025') and from the last Internet Archive snapshot of the old URL (03/10/2023). No unibz page states the transition date in words.

(5) LATE-SESSION ADMISSION COUNT. 28 EU applicants were admitted in the Late session against a nominal 10 late places. The explanation — carry-over of Early Bird places not secured — follows from the published carry-over rule but is an inference; unibz publishes no attrition data. Flagged inline in places_quotas.

(6) SCORE SCALE DISCREPANCY. The four criteria sum to a maximum of 102 points (70 + 2 laude + 10 language + 20 prior knowledge), and the Late list's top score is exactly 102.00, confirming the arithmetic. Yet the signed decree words the floor as 'il punteggio minimo di 60/100 punti' — 60 out of 100. Both documents agree the floor is 60 points; the '/100' is best read as loose phrasing rather than a different scale.

(7) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS UNCONFIRMED. The €1,680–€6,960 range and any 27/30 merit threshold in the field schema could not be confirmed on any page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts annually.

(8) CERTIFICATE HOME-EDITION SCOPE. The '* Also accepted as "home edition"' asterisk appears against several English providers in Resolution 16/2026's multi-column table but its exact per-cell scope could not be confirmed, and no equivalent marking was observed for the Italian or German providers that matter most here. Verify with language.centre@unibz.it.

(9) EXPLICIT NOT-APPLICABLE FINDINGS, recorded positively rather than left blank so a later reader does not infer 'unknown': NO interview, NO entrance exam of any kind, NO TOLC/SAT/CENT-S, NO GMAT/GRE bonus, NO Webometrics bonus, NO portfolio or motivation letter or video, NO OFA, and NO minimum grade average.

The programme-page slug omits 'and' ('master-public-policy-innovative-governance') while both PDF slugs include it ('master-in-public-policy-and-innovative-governance'), so deriving the PDF path from the page slug 404s.
